title: Keep every TypeScript file at a 10% or higher comment ratio

facts.note: Extension .ts/.tsx of any scanned file, changed or unchanged.

Source categories: test files and vendored/build directories are outside the scan. Illustrative globs (e.g. *.test.ts, *.spec.ts, vendor/, node_modules/, dist/, build/) are non-exhaustive; the detector's own exclusion set is authoritative.
Requires bun_ts_metrics_detector to compute the per-file comment ratio and report a below-10% finding.

fires: Any scanned .ts/.tsx file that is not a test file and not under a vendored/build directory has comment lines under 10% of its non-blank lines, whether or not it was edited in this task.
The metrics detector reports REFACTOR-QUALITY-COMMENTS-TS-001 for a non-test, non-vendored, non-build TypeScript/TSX file in the scanned tree.
A new non-test .ts/.tsx module outside vendored/build directories is written whose comment lines are below 10% of its non-blank lines.
doesNotFire: A test file has no comments.
A file under a vendored or build output directory has a low comment ratio.
A TypeScript/TSX file already at or above a 10% comment ratio, regardless of whether its comments are a header or explanatory (quality is a review concern, not this trigger).

given: An in-scope .ts/.tsx file (not a test, not vendored/build), changed or not
when: its comment lines (line, block, `*` continuations) fall below 10% of non-blank lines
then: Raise the comment ratio to >=10% by writing down the decisions and constraints invisible to a reader.
prefer: Diagnose: module purpose and owned responsibility; non-obvious invariants, upstream/compatibility constraints, failure semantics; obvious implementations intentionally not chosen.
Document why a choice exists, which invariant a block keeps, or which external constraint forces the shape.
Use a concise module/GREEN header giving real purpose and runtime context; with a few explanatory lines it clears the floor.
Place the explanation next to the decision it clarifies.
avoid: Comments restating the next line of code.
Filler, generated prose, repeated headings, or artificially split comment lines to raise the ratio.
Commenting out dead code instead of deleting it.
Changing cohesive code solely to manipulate the denominator.
Stale or misleading comments; any behavior change (tests stay green).
unless: Test files; vendored/build directories (outside the scan).
why: Comment-free files almost always hide unwritten non-obvious decisions. 10% is a floor against absence, not a quality measure or prose quota; numerator-padding filler makes the source worse.
evidence: The comment-ratio finding (REFACTOR-QUALITY-COMMENTS-TS-001) is gone for the file.
Every added comment conveys information not already obvious from the code.
No stale or misleading comments were introduced.
Behavior remains unchanged and tests stay green.
The refactor introduces no new ATDD Bun violations.
verifier_detail: comment_ratio = comment lines / all non-blank lines; threshold: ratio >= 0.10 for every in-scope TypeScript/TSX file.
Comment lines counted: line comments, block comments, and continuation lines beginning `*` inside a block comment — counted against all non-blank lines.
Blank lines are excluded from both numerator and denominator.
Test files and vendored/build directories are outside the scan.
Detector: bun_ts_metrics_detector (native Bun), numerically identical to the python-pytest sibling's detector.
Ten percent is low enough that any file with a real header and a few explanatory lines clears it.

The ratio cannot tell a good comment from a bad one; it catches the file that documents nothing (floor_against_absence). Reviewers judge whether added comments carry real design context and flag filler/restating comments added to game the numerator; a ratio is a blunt instrument for a non-quantitative quality. Treat it as a sensor for missing design context, not a prose quota; a successful repair leaves readers information the code itself cannot communicate.
Severity 2; disposition strict (fails on every finding).
audit: Source name: TypeScript files carry at least a 10% comment ratio
Stack-neutral obligation; NATIVE BUN detector transcribed from the python-pytest sibling `coder.refactor.quality-comments-typescript` and verified numerically identical.
Terms: comment_ratio; floor_against_absence (what this rule is).
